title: Clocktower Horologist
premise: A long timing drama in the city clocktower. Technician Hanshuang and apprentice Doudou guard the astronomical escapement wheel; Doudou and Aheng look nearly alike but wear different neckwear; the brass inspection cradle crashes and must be avoided; the timing log, count memory, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_horologist: A forty-year-old clocktower technician in a gray felt newsboy cap and gray felt work clothes, a magnifying glass hung on his chest, long fingers stained with machine oil.
states.cane_sprain: The same Hanshuang: right ankle old injury, leaning on a cane made from a broken ruler, gray felt work clothes worn through at the knees, magnifying glass still hung on his chest.
states.silent_death: Hanshuang has closed his eyes and passed away, lying quietly on a folding cot in the clocktower machine room, gray felt work clothes covering his chest.

states.young_apprentice: A fifteen-year-old apprentice girl in deep-blue overalls, a small pocket-watch chain at her waist, keen eyes.
states.adult_technician: A woman technician in her early twenties, still with the pocket-watch chain and deep-blue overalls, upright build, able to calibrate the whole clockwork alone.

states.intact: A palm-sized astronomical escapement wheel, star-scale marks on the rim, gem bearings flashing, meshing smoothly with the pallet fork.
states.broken_teeth: The same astronomical escapement wheel missing two teeth, bearings blackened by machine oil, trembling lightly as it swings.
states.teeth_replaced: After new teeth are fitted, the astronomical escapement wheel runs smooth again; the new teeth are slightly lighter in color, star-scale marks still clear.

states.intact: A lacquered-cloth-cover timing log recording daily rate error, winding times, and tower-clock maintenance notes.
states.oil_stained: The same timing log soaked through with machine oil, cover sticky, error figures blurred into black blotches.

states.intact: A brass inspection cradle with a number carved on the guardrail, hoist rope clipped to the clocktower gallery rail, able to rise beside the clock face.
states.crashed: After falling from the rail, the brass inspection cradle has a twisted guardrail, cracked number plate, and hoist rope spilled in loose coils.

states.young_rival: A youth whose face closely resembles Doudou's, but wearing a silver-gray scarf and charcoal-black overalls, arrogant expression.
states.remade_face: After remaking his look, Aheng still wears the silver-gray scarf, a metal scrape mark on his brow ridge, charcoal-black overalls swapped for a leather-buckle cut.

segments.action: At dusk, Hanshuang pushes open the clocktower machine room iron door and sets the astronomical escapement wheel at the center of the timing bench.
Five brass inspection gas lamps hang in a row under the machine-room beams; Hanshuang polishes each glass shade that reflects gear shadows.
Two tower clock bells hang above the machine room; Hanshuang gently nudges a hammer rod, letting the low chime roll among the gears.
Hanshuang seats the astronomical escapement wheel into the pallet fork, watching whether the swing catches mid-tooth.
He drips a little watch oil onto a gear by the timing bench and listens as the whole train slowly meshes.
Hanshuang unties the wax cord and opens the lacquered-cloth-cover timing log.
He notes today's rate error, mainspring tension, and hourly strike deviation in carbon ink.
Hanshuang closes the log and returns the astronomical escapement wheel to the velvet pad so the teeth will not bend.
On the morning clocktower gallery, Hanshuang greets young Doudou pushing the brass inspection cradle in.

segments.action: Months later on a stormy night, Hanshuang keeps watch alone in the clocktower machine room, the astronomical escapement wheel resting on the velvet pad.
He opens the timing log and finds machine oil leaked from the gear box; the lacquered-cloth cover is sticky, error figures blurred into black blotches.

segments.action: Through the long timing season, Hanshuang winds, listens to the beat, and calibrates the hour day after day in the machine room.
Another snowy night, he pulls the gray felt work clothes tight and keeps watch by the gear train for the city clock chime.
Spring mist fills the air; Hanshuang opens the gallery window to check that the clock hands are free of condensed water.
At high summer noon, he wipes copper filings squeezed from gear roots by heat expansion.
Autumn wind enters the machine room; the clock-hammer haul ropes gently bump the wall.
At dawn, Hanshuang patrols along the clocktower gallery; the brass inspection cradle rests to the right of the clock face.
He bends to check the cradle guardrail and rail safety catch, confirming the hoist rope is not worn through.
Hanshuang gathers small gears scattered on the gallery into a toolbox so they will not roll into the drain channel.
A temporary iron scaffold lift is pushed in from the stair landing; the iron frame has no brass guardrail number and cannot hang beside the clock face.
Rain lashes the huge clock face; the gallery rail screeches in the wind.
Hanshuang has just reseated the astronomical escapement wheel in the movement when two teeth shear off under a misaligned shock.

state.appearance: The same astronomical escapement wheel missing two teeth, bearings blackened by machine oil, trembling lightly as it swings.

segments.action: The brass inspection cradle is shoved off the clock face by the gale; the hoist rope thrashes violently on the rail.
The hoist rope finally snaps; the brass inspection cradle plunges from the gallery, guardrail twisted, number plate cracked.

segments.action: Hanshuang cradles the broken-toothed escapement wheel back into the machine room; rain drips from his cap brim onto the timing bench.

segments.action: On a wall hook hangs the hoist rope torn from the brass inspection cradle; Hanshuang leaves it there a long while.
Hanshuang takes one of the five inspection gas lamps from under the beams to light the oil-blurred error table in the log.
He places the cracked number plate from the brass inspection cradle into a parts box and closes the velvet lid.
Weeks later, Hanshuang brings in an old clockmaker to remove the two sheared teeth on the timing bench.

segments.action: A wooden ladder cart is pushed onto the gallery; it holds only a folding wooden ladder and toolbox—not the crashed brass inspection cradle.
The municipal clock officer steps beside Hanshuang to inspect the clock face; both wear gray felt newsboy caps, backs nearly alike.
The clock officer points at the wooden ladder cart to schedule tomorrow's face washing; Hanshuang keeps listening to the tower clock's return swing.
Square news girl Lingling climbs the gallery to deliver papers; her light-brown overalls from afar look like young Doudou's deep-blue ones.
Lingling tries to grip the safety rope; Hanshuang shakes his head, noting her round glasses—she is not Doudou after all.
Years later at dusk, Hanshuang leans on the broken-ruler cane and slowly enters the stopped old clocktower.
